abstractParagraphs: Modern cloud-native and microservice applications expose core business logic and sensitive multi-tenant data through HTTP Application Programming Interfaces (APIs). Organizations routinely configure defensive controls—such as API-key authentication, rate limiting, Web Application Firewall (WAF) filters, Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) guards, and upstream timeouts—under the assumption that configuration alone guarantees runtime protection. In practice, concurrency race conditions in rate limiters, middleware ordering defects, upstream dependency latency spikes, and cross-tenant authorization oversights frequently invalidate those assumptions under real traffic.

FortiX is an integrated API Security and Resilience Verification Platform built around a closed-loop engineering lifecycle: PROTECT → BREAK → OBSERVE → PROVE → IMPROVE. Rather than treating gateway protection, fault injection, and compliance reporting as disconnected tools, FortiX unifies (1) an HTTP reverse-proxy enforcement plane (/proxy/:routeId/*) implementing SHA-256/bcrypt scoped API-key validation, SSRF/DNS-rebinding defenses, multi-decoded SQLi/XSS/traversal WAF inspection, and atomic Redis Lua token-bucket rate limiting; (2) FortiX API Studio, a self-contained zero-backend API builder seeded with a canonical 100-record e-commerce Products dataset and OpenAPI 3.0.3 export; (3) an asynchronous BullMQ experiment engine that executes bounded latency, HTTP 5xx, timeout, and rate-limit burst workloads across three distinct observation windows (BASELINE, INJECTION, and RECOVERY); (4) a deterministic Verification Engine synchronized via a telemetry flush barrier that produces non-vacuous PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE verdicts backed by SHA-256 integrity-hashed PDF compliance reports; and (5) an integrated In-App Video Learning Center (FTX-LEARN-001) guiding operators across the complete verification workflow.

The platform is implemented in TypeScript 5.8 on Node.js 22 (Express 4.21 backend, React 19 + Vite 6.2 control-plane SPA) backed by a normalized 23-table PostgreSQL 15 relational schema managed with Drizzle ORM 0.45 and hardened with PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies on 17 tenant-owned and user-owned tables, alongside Redis 7 for Lua rate-limit state, Redis Streams telemetry ingestion (fortix:stream:metrics and fortix:stream:security), multi-replica key-revocation Pub/Sub (fortix:api-key:revoked:v1), and BullMQ job queues. Operator authentication (FTX-AUTH-001) provides HttpOnly session cookies, rotating Remember-Me refresh token families with reuse detection, double-submit CSRF protection, and multi-step 6-digit HMAC-SHA256 OTP account recovery.

Empirical validation across the repository confirms 35 passing Vitest unit and integration test suites (269/269 passing assertions) and 13 passing Playwright end-to-end and security browser/API specifications (46.3s), demonstrating deterministic enforcement and verifiable evidence generation.

sections.title: Problem Definition (Identification of Needs)

blocks.text: Contemporary software architectures—spanning financial payment processors, e-commerce catalogs, healthcare portals, and Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) platforms—rely on RESTful HTTP APIs as their primary operational boundary. Unlike monolithic web applications where internal procedure calls remained isolated inside a single process memory space, API-first architectures expose parameterized network endpoints directly to web browsers, mobile applications, partner integrations, and automated adversaries.

Engineering teams typically respond to this exposure by deploying middleware controls: authentication checks, role-based access rules, request rate limiters, payload validators, and upstream HTTP timeouts. However, operational incidents repeatedly demonstrate a fundamental engineering gap: configuring a security or resilience control in code or YAML does not prove that the control behaves deterministically under concurrent adversarial traffic or upstream degradation.

items: Authentication and Authorization Drift: Endpoints intended to require scoped API keys or tenant ownership checks frequently suffer from Broken Object Level Authorization (OWASP API1:2023), unrevoked cached credentials after key rotation, or session tokens that remain usable after password resets.

Non-Atomic Rate Limiting Under Concurrency: Naive read-modify-write rate counters in application memory or non-transactional caches allow concurrent request bursts to bypass configured Requests-Per-Minute (RPM) ceilings due to race conditions.

Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) and Encoded Payloads: Reverse proxies that accept user-configured upstream URLs without validating private RFC 1918 ranges, loopback interfaces, cloud metadata IPs (169.254.169.254), and DNS-rebinding resolutions expose internal infrastructure, while single-pass string filters miss multi-encoded SQL injection (SQLi) and Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vectors.

Unverified Resilience and Silent Cascading Failures: Upstream microservices inevitably experience latency spikes, HTTP 502/503 errors, or hung TCP sockets. Without controlled fault injection and post-fault recovery measurement, operators cannot know whether gateway timeouts isolate the failure or whether downstream pools remain wedged.

Telemetry Flush Races and Vacuous Verification: Even when teams run ad-hoc load scripts, asynchronous metric pipelines often lag behind verification queries—causing automated checks to evaluate zero rows or incomplete samples and emit misleading "green" pass statuses.

Onboarding Friction in Security Tooling: Evaluating an API security gateway traditionally requires deploying a separate external microservice first and reading external documentation, creating friction during development, security testing, and academic evaluation.

blocks.title: Core Engineering Distinction Addressed by FortiX
blocks.text: Configuring a control declares intent; testing sends synthetic stimuli; observing records runtime telemetry; proving evaluates complete, synchronized baseline, fault-injection, and recovery observations against explicit SLA rules to produce tamper-evident PASS, FAIL, or INCONCLUSIVE evidence.

subsections.title: Problem Statement and Proposed FortiX Solution

blocks.text: Problem Statement: Organizations operating HTTP APIs lack a unified, self-contained engineering platform capable of enforcing multi-layered gateway protections, executing bounded fault-injection and rate-limit experiments against authorized routes, synchronizing asynchronous telemetry without race conditions, and deterministically proving whether security and resilience policies hold across baseline, active-fault, and post-fault recovery windows.

Proposed System (FortiX): FortiX is an integrated API Security and Resilience Verification Platform structured around five tightly coupled stages—PROTECT, BREAK, OBSERVE, PROVE, and IMPROVE—augmented by FortiX API Studio (so operators can create realistic data-backed REST APIs inside the platform itself) and an integrated In-App Video Learning Center (FTX-LEARN-001) guiding operators step-by-step.

blocks.text: Important Positioning Note: FortiX is engineered as a focused verification-first API security gateway and resilience testbed for academic defense, security engineering validation, and small-to-medium service environments. It does not claim to replace hyperscale commercial CDN edge networks, kernel-level L3/L4 DDoS scrubbers, or full OWASP Core Rule Set enterprise appliances.

subsections.title: Objectives, Scope Governance, Assumptions, and Out-of-Scope Boundaries

items: Enforce layered pre-upstream API protection (scoped API keys, SSRF/DNS-rebinding guards, multi-decoded SQLi/XSS/path-traversal WAF inspection, and atomic Redis Lua rate limiting) with sub-millisecond in-process fast paths.

Provide hardened operator authentication (FTX-AUTH-001) supporting email or verified E.164 phone sign-in, Remember-Me refresh session rotation, active session revocation, and 6-digit HMAC-SHA256 OTP password recovery.
Eliminate external demo dependencies via FortiX API Studio, enabling zero-code creation of multi-resource CRUD APIs pre-populated with a deterministic 100-record Store Products catalog.
Execute bounded, authorized resilience experiments (latency injection, HTTP 5xx failure injection, upstream timeout simulation, and rate-limit burst verification) via BullMQ background workers.
Guarantee deterministic verification by synchronizing Redis Stream telemetry persistence prior to evaluation and enforcing baseline, injection, and recovery sample sufficiency rules.
Produce downloadable SHA-256 verified PDF evidence reports, signed outbound webhook notifications, resilience posture scoring, and guided in-app video tutorials.

blocks.text: Scope Governance & Explicit Out-of-Scope Boundaries: Every retained module in FortiX maps directly to the Protect → Break → Observe → Prove → Improve lifecycle. Capabilities outside current implementation scope—specifically Kubernetes Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) and Helm operators, kernel-level volumetric L3/L4 DDoS mitigation, gRPC/GraphQL AST depth inspection, and hardware FIDO2/WebAuthn passkeys—are explicitly excluded from current claims and documented as future work in Section 5.2.

subsections.title: Six-Dimensional Engineering Evaluation of Core Technologies

items: Node.js 22 & TypeScript 5.8 — (1) Intro: Event-driven JavaScript runtime paired with structural static typing. (2) Purpose: Powers HTTP reverse proxying, cryptographic hashing/HMAC, probe generation, and verification logic. (3) Why Selected: High concurrency for I/O-bound gateway proxying and single-language sharing of domain types between backend and React UI. (4) Integration: Compiles via esbuild into dist/server.cjs and dist/worker.cjs. (5) Benefits: Fast startup, native WebCrypto/Node crypto, unified codebase. (6) Limitations: Single-threaded CPU loop requires offloading bcrypt caching and running workers in a separate process.

Express 4.21 — (1) Intro: Minimalist HTTP routing and middleware framework. (2) Purpose: Hosts /api/auth/*, /api/control/*, and wildcard /proxy/:routeId/* pipelines. (3) Why Selected: Deterministic middleware ordering—vital for ensuring authentication and WAF execute strictly before fault injection. (4) Integration: Co-hosted on the same HTTP server as Socket.IO and http-proxy-middleware. (5) Benefits: Mature ecosystem (cookie-parser, cors, express-rate-limit). (6) Limitations: Requires explicit async error handling to avoid unhandled rejections.

React 19, Vite 6.2 & Tailwind CSS 4 — (1) Intro: Component-based declarative UI library with modern ESM build tooling. (2) Purpose: Implements Login, 3-step OTP Recovery, Command Dashboard, API Studio, Security Policies, Threats, Experiments, Verifications, Resilience, Topology, Learning Center, and Settings. (3) Why Selected: Instant state transitions, clean hook composition, and zero-runtime CSS overhead. (4) Integration: Communicates via src/lib/api.ts with credentials: "include", X-CSRF-Token injection, and silent /api/auth/refresh retry. (5) Benefits: Responsive operator workflow and Recharts latency visualization. (6) Limitations: Client-side SPA requires strict backend authorization because browser code is untrusted.

PostgreSQL 15 & Drizzle ORM 0.45 — (1) Intro: ACID-compliant open-source RDBMS paired with a SQL-centric TypeScript ORM. (2) Purpose: Authoritative system of record for all 23 tables. (3) Why Selected: Native JSONB support for flexible verification evidence/Studio records, atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING for single-use tokens, and engine-level Row-Level Security (RLS). (4) Integration: Managed via src/db/index.ts with automatic pg-mem fallback for isolated unit tests. (5) Benefits: Zero SQL injection via bound parameters and transparent migration SQL files. (6) Limitations: High-frequency telemetry writes require Redis Stream batching to prevent connection pool saturation.

Redis 7 & BullMQ 6.3 — (1) Intro: In-memory data structure server and Redis-backed distributed job queue. (2) Purpose: Executes atomic Lua token-bucket rate limiting, buffers telemetry streams, broadcasts revoked API keys, and orchestrates multi-phase chaos jobs. (3) Why Selected: Server-side Lua scripts execute atomically without lock contention across multiple gateway replicas. (4) Integration: Connected via ioredis in src/redis.ts, src/rate-limit/redis.ts, and src/experiments/worker.ts. (5) Benefits: Sub-millisecond rate-limit decisions and durable job retries with DLQ inspection. (6) Limitations: Ephemeral memory footprint requires AOF persistence (--appendonly yes) and explicit TTL hygiene.

Zod 4.5, Pino 10.3, PDFKit 0.20, Vitest 5.0 & Playwright 1.63 — (1) Intro: Validation, observability, reporting, and testing toolchain. (2) Purpose: Enforces strict DTO contracts at trust boundaries, emits redacted JSON logs, renders tamper-evident PDFs, and continuously verifies security/verification invariants. (3) Why Selected: Eliminates runtime type coercion bugs and proves end-to-end browser + proxy behavior. (4) Integration: Wired into Express routes, verification artifacts, and CI npm scripts. (5) Benefits: High defect detection (caught all four historical verification engine defects). (6) Limitations: Headless browser E2E suites require Chromium binaries in the test container.

sections.title: Sequence Diagrams and Deployment Topology

blocks.text: This section documents all nine critical runtime workflows in FortiX using synchronous solid arrows and asynchronous/response dashed arrows, followed by the multi-container production deployment topology.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 1 — Operator Login, Remember-Me Token Rotation, and Multi-Step OTP Password Recovery
blocks.sourceNote: Implements FTX-AUTH-001 across src/api/auth.ts, src/auth/sessions.ts, and src/auth/recovery.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 1 Explanation (Figure 2.7): During login (steps 1–5), the Auth Router resolves the identifier by normalized email or verified E.164 phone, verifies the bcrypt hash, creates a refresh_tokens family row (30 days when rememberMe=true, 12 hours otherwise), and sets HttpOnly cookies (fortix_session, fortix_refresh) plus fortix_csrf. During account recovery (steps 6–16), /forgot-password generates a 6-digit OTP, stores only its keyed HMAC-SHA256 digest in recovery_challenges, and verifies HTTP 2xx provider delivery. On /verify-reset-otp, an atomic conditional SQL update marks consumed_at and issues a single-use RESET_AUTHORIZATION token. Finally, /reset-password updates password_hash and revokes every refresh token and active JWT session family for the user.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 2 — Gateway Reverse-Proxy Request Processing and Credential Sanitization
blocks.sourceNote: Implements /proxy/:routeId/* in src/gateway/index.ts and src/gateway/ssrf.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 2 Explanation (Figure 2.8): Every incoming proxy request receives a correlation X-Request-ID. After SSRF target validation (safeDnsLookup preventing DNS rebinding to internal IPs), API-key authentication, and WAF payload inspection succeed, the gateway strips X-API-Key and any fx_* Authorization header so FortiX credentials never leak to external upstreams. Upstream latency and status codes are captured on response finish and pushed asynchronously to fortix:stream:metrics.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 3 — Scoped API-Key Validation, SHA-256 Digest Caching, and Pub/Sub Revocation
blocks.sourceNote: Implements HashedApiKeyCache in src/gateway/index.ts and publishApiKeyInvalidation() in src/lib/key-invalidation.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 3 Explanation (Figure 2.9): On a cache miss, the gateway extracts keyId from fx_live_<keyId>_<secret>, loads the project-scoped row from api_keys, verifies non-revocation, expiration, required route scopes, and bcrypt.compare(secret, secretHash), and caches non-sensitive metadata keyed by SHA-256(rawKey). When an operator revokes or deletes a key, publishApiKeyInvalidation() broadcasts on Redis channel fortix:api-key:revoked:v1 so all gateway replicas evict the cached digest immediately.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 4 — Atomic Redis Lua Token-Bucket Rate-Limit Enforcement
blocks.sourceNote: Implements checkRateLimit() in src/rate-limit/redis.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 4 Explanation (Figure 2.10): To prevent race conditions under concurrent burst traffic, checkRateLimit() evaluates an embedded Lua script inside Redis using EVAL on key ratelimit:{routeId}:{identifier}. Within a single atomic Redis execution step, the script reads tokens and last_refill via HMGET, calculates elapsed token replenishment capped at route rate_limit_rpm, decrements 1 token if available, updates state with HMSET and PEXPIRE, and returns {allowed, remaining}. Exhausted buckets immediately return HTTP 429 and log a throttled telemetry observation.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 5 — Experiment Creation, BullMQ Queuing, and Three-Phase Execution
blocks.sourceNote: Implements src/api/experiments.ts and src/experiments/worker.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 5 Explanation (Figure 2.11): Creating an experiment validates route ownership and bounded parameters (durationMs <= 60,000 ms), persists status=QUEUED, and enqueues a BullMQ job. The worker mints a 15-minute ephemeral fx_test_* API key, executes 5 clean BASELINE probes while fault injection is inactive, transitions status to RUNNING (activating gateway fault injection on that route) while sending tagged INJECTION probe waves, and finally transitions to ANALYZING to record 5 post-fault RECOVERY probes.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 6 — Bounded Fault Injection, Operator Abort, and Guaranteed Cleanup
blocks.sourceNote: Illustrates fail-safe try/finally cleanup in src/experiments/worker.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 6 Explanation (Figure 2.12): If an operator triggers POST /api/control/experiments/:id/cancel or an unexpected exception occurs mid-run, the API immediately sets status=CANCELLED and invalidates the gateway experiment cache. Before each probe wave, the worker checks isExperimentCancelled(), exits cleanly, and executes its finally block—unconditionally deleting the temporary fx_test_* API key row and clearing any cached fault state.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 7 & 8 — Telemetry Stream Flush Barrier and Evidence-Based Verification
blocks.sourceNote: Implements flushTelemetryBarrier() and verifyPolicy() in src/verification/engine.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 7 & 8 Explanation (Figure 2.13): Immediately after probe execution completes, VerificationEngine invokes flushTelemetryBarrier() so buffered fortix:stream:metrics entries are committed to metric_logs before SQL evaluation begins—eliminating the classic async telemetry race condition. Observations are partitioned into BASELINE, INJECTION, and RECOVERY windows using exact probe request IDs and timestamp bounds. If expected probe coverage falls below 80% or zero samples exist, the engine refuses to emit a vacuous PASS and instead records INCONCLUSIVE; otherwise it evaluates deterministic policy thresholds to persist PASS or FAIL alongside a SHA-256 PDF report.

blocks.caption: Sequence Diagram 9 — FortiX API Studio 100-Product Provisioning and Protected Gateway CRUD
blocks.sourceNote: Implements src/api/studio.ts and src/studio/target-handler.ts.

blocks.text: Workflow 9 Explanation (Figure 2.14): Selecting the Store Products (100) template in API Studio creates an internal route (targetUrl = http://fortix-studio.internal/studio/<apiId>), attaches WAF/SSRF/rate-limit policies, seeds 100 deterministic Indian e-commerce products into studio_records, and issues a ready-to-use scoped API key. Subsequent GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE calls traverse the exact same /proxy/:routeId/* enforcement pipeline before reaching handleStudioUpstreamRequest(), allowing complete security and chaos verification with zero external services.

subsections.title: Normalization, JSONB Trade-Offs, Indexing, Transactions, and Row-Level Security (RLS)

items: First, Second, and Third Normal Form (1NF–3NF): Core relational entities—users, organizations, projects, api_routes, api_keys, security_policies, experiments, verifications, refresh_tokens, recovery_challenges, learning_tutorials, and learning_progress—satisfy 3NF. Every non-key attribute depends solely on the table UUID primary key without transitive dependencies between non-key attributes. Controlled denormalization of project_id onto studio_resources, studio_records, and webhook_deliveries is deliberately employed so PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies and B-tree indexes can filter tenant rows in O(log N) without three-table joins on every request.

Justified JSONB Columns: PostgreSQL JSONB is used strictly where schemas are inherently polymorphic or structured arrays: Studio dynamic resource payloads (studio_records.data), experiment fault configurations (experiments.config), verification phase histograms (verifications.observed), tutorial step checklists (learning_tutorials.steps), and audit diffs (audit_logs.diff). All JSONB writes are validated beforehand by Zod schemas or validateStudioRecordPayload().

Composite B-Tree Indexing Strategy: Hot read paths use targeted composite indexes—route_time_idx(route_id, timestamp) for time-windowed verification queries, threat_route_time_idx(route_id, timestamp) for WAF dashboards, refresh_tokens_family_idx(family_id) for instant token-family revocation, recovery_challenges_user_purpose_idx(user_id, purpose, created_at) for OTP cooldown checks, studio_records_resource_record_id_idx(resource_id, record_id) for O(log N) CRUD lookups, and learning_progress_user_tutorial_idx(user_id, tutorial_id) for idempotent progress upserts.

Referential Integrity & Atomic Transactions: Deleting a project cascades cleanly across routes, keys, policies, Studio APIs, experiments, and logs, whereas deleting an experiment sets metric_logs.experiment_id to NULL (ON DELETE SET NULL) so historical route traffic metrics remain intact. Single-use token consumption (consumeAuthActionToken and verifyPasswordRecoveryOtp) uses atomic conditional UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING * statements to prevent race conditions under concurrent requests.

Engine-Level Tenant Isolation (PostgreSQL RLS): In drizzle/postgres_rls_policies.sql and withTenantContext() (src/db/index.ts), FortiX creates non-superuser role fortix_app (NOBYPASSRLS), binds set_config('app.current_user_id', userId, true) inside transactions, and enforces ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY across all 17 tenant-owned and user-owned tables as defense-in-depth behind application-level project ownership guards.

blocks.title: Sample 1 — Rotating Remember-Me Refresh Sessions & Reuse Detection

blocks.text: Walkthrough & Security Analysis (src/auth/sessions.ts): (1) Purpose: Rotates opaque refresh tokens across browser restarts while detecting stolen token replay. (2) Logical Blocks: Hashes incoming cookie value with SHA-256; checks whether replacedById or revokedAt is already set; if replayed, revokes every row in familyId and calls revokeSessionFamilySid() in src/lib/jwt-security.ts; otherwise inserts a successor token and links replacedById. blocks.title: Sample 2 — Domain-Separated HMAC-SHA256 OTP Verification & Atomic Consumption

blocks.text: Walkthrough & Security Analysis (src/auth/recovery.ts): (1) Purpose: Verifies 6-digit account recovery OTPs without storing plaintext codes or permitting brute-force/race attacks. (2) Logical Blocks: Derives a domain-separated HMAC key via getOtpHmacSecret(), binds challengeId and purpose into computeOtpHmac(), compares digests via crypto.timingSafeEqual, locks after 5 failed attempts, and executes atomic conditional UPDATE ... WHERE consumed_at IS NULL RETURNING * so 10 concurrent identical POST requests yield exactly one resetAuthorization token. (3) Anti-Enumeration: Unknown identifiers receive a HMAC-tagged synthetic challenge UUID so response timing and payload shape are indistinguishable. (4) Tests: Verified in tests/unit/ftx-auth-001.test.ts and tests/e2e/auth-recovery.spec.ts.

blocks.title: Sample 3 — Atomic Redis Lua Token-Bucket Rate Limiter
blocks.code:
const TOKEN_BUCKET_LUA = `
local key = KEYS[1]
local capacity = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local refill_rate = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local now_ms = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local requested = tonumber(ARGV[4])
local ttl_ms = tonumber(ARGV[5])

local data = redis.call('HMGET', key, 'tokens', 'last_refill')
local tokens = tonumber(data[1])
local last_refill = tonumber(data[2])
if tokens == nil then
  tokens = capacity
  last_refill = now_ms
else
  local elapsed = math.max(0, now_ms - last_refill) / 1000.0
  tokens = math.min(capacity, tokens + (elapsed * refill_rate))
  last_refill = now_ms
end
if tokens >= requested then
  tokens = tokens - requested
  redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', tokens, 'last_refill', last_refill)
  redis.call('PEXPIRE', key, ttl_ms)
  return {1, math.floor(tokens)}
else
  redis.call('HMSET', key, 'tokens', tokens, 'last_refill', last_refill)
  redis.call('PEXPIRE', key, ttl_ms)
  return {0, 0}
end`;

blocks.text: Walkthrough & Security Analysis (src/rate-limit/redis.ts): (1) Purpose: Enforces exact per-route RPM limits across concurrent gateway workers without read-modify-write race conditions. items: 1. Authentication: Dual-identifier login (email or verified E.164 phone) with dummy bcrypt comparison on unknown users to mitigate timing enumeration.
2. Authorization & RBAC: Role hierarchy (ADMIN, DEVELOPER, VIEWER) enforced server-side via src/middleware/entitlements.ts, src/api/admin.ts, and project BOLA guards.
3. Password Handling: Hashed exclusively with bcryptjs (cost factor 10); never stored in localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies, or logs.
4. API-Key Protection: Raw fx_live_<id>_<secret> shown once; DB stores bcrypt secret_hash; gateway caches SHA-256 digest with secretHash stripped and fortix:api-key:revoked:v1 Pub/Sub eviction.
5. Session Management: Short-lived access JWT in HttpOnly cookie + rotating refresh token families (12h standard / 30d Remember Me) with reuse detection and global revocation on password reset.
6. Input Validation: Strict Zod schemas on every REST route, Studio dynamic field validation, and allowlisted tutorial media URL validation.
7. Rate Limiting: Express auth rate limiter on /api/auth/* and atomic Redis Lua token bucket on /proxy/:routeId/*.
8. SQL Injection Prevention: 100% parameterized queries via Drizzle ORM plus gateway WAF multi-decoded SQLi signature blocking.
9. SSRF Protection: Blocks private RFC 1918, loopback, link-local/cloud metadata (169.254.169.254), and DNS-rebinding resolutions via safeDnsLookup (src/gateway/ssrf.ts).
10. CORS & CSRF: Strict origin allowlist with credentials support and double-submit CSRF validation (fortix_csrf cookie matched against X-CSRF-Token header) on cookie-authenticated mutations.
11. Multi-Tenant Isolation: Dual-layer enforcement combining application-level project ownership checks and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security (RLS) policies across 17 tenant/user tables.
12. Secret Management: Fail-fast startup checks in production requiring cryptographic JWT_SECRET, OTP_HMAC_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, and REDIS_URL.
13. Logging & Redaction: Pino logger configured with explicit redact paths stripping authorization headers, cookies, password fields, OTPs, and raw keys.
14. Experiment Authorization & Blast Radius: Experiments execute only against routes owned by the caller project, post-authentication, with hard duration caps (<=60s) and guaranteed cleanup.
15. Resource Limits: JSON body size caps, bounded in-memory caches (max 5,000 API keys), and upstream proxy socket timeouts.

16. Error Handling & Known Security Boundaries: Central error middleware suppresses stack traces in production. Honest Limitation Disclosure: FortiX does not yet implement hardware WebAuthn/FIDO2 MFA, kernel-level L3/L4 DDoS mitigation, or external KMS envelope encryption; SMS/Email OTP delivery in production depends on configuring external HTTPS provider webhooks.

sections.title: Definitions of Core Security, Gateway, and Resilience Terms

blocks.caption: Technical Glossary of FortiX Domain Concepts
rows: Intermediary HTTP enforcement server (/proxy/:routeId/*) that authenticates, inspects, rate-limits, and sanitizes client requests before forwarding to upstream services.
Compact HMAC-SHA256 signed session claim token stored in HttpOnly cookies and bound to a refresh session family (sid).
Client credential formatted as fx_live_<id>_<secret> whose secret is verified via bcrypt and restricted to explicit project routes and scopes.
Permission model restricting control-plane operations across ADMIN, DEVELOPER, and VIEWER roles.
Isolation architecture ensuring one organization/project cannot read or mutate another tenant's routes, keys, or records at both API and PostgreSQL Row-Level Security layers.
Traffic-policing algorithm executed atomically via Redis Lua script that replenishes capacity at a fixed RPM rate and rejects excess bursts with HTTP 429.
Deliberate, bounded introduction of latency, HTTP 5xx errors, or upstream timeouts on authorized routes after authentication to test resilience.
Pre-fault (5 probes) and post-fault (5 probes) observation intervals used to establish normal behavior and prove clean recovery after chaos stops.
Synchronization step (flushTelemetryBarrier) draining asynchronous Redis Stream metrics into PostgreSQL before verification queries execute.
Response latency thresholds below which 50%, 95%, and 99% of observed gateway requests complete.
Deterministic verification outcomes: PASS (SLA satisfied with >=80% sample coverage), FAIL (SLA breached), INCONCLUSIVE (insufficient telemetry samples—preventing vacuous passes).

rows: OTP delivery providers (src/auth/providers.ts) implement production HTTPS webhook adapters with local outbox fallback in development; real inbox/SMS delivery requires configuring external SMTP/SMS webhook credentials.
Gateway WAF inspects multi-decoded SQLi, XSS, and path-traversal signatures effectively for REST JSON APIs, but is not a full OWASP ModSecurity CRS behavioral anomaly engine.
Docker Compose deploys single-primary PostgreSQL 15 and Redis 7 instances; active-active multi-region replication and automated failover are outside current scope.
Gateway proxying and API Studio target HTTP/1.1 REST/JSON workloads; gRPC (HTTP/2 trailers) and GraphQL AST depth limiting are not currently implemented.
